history.period: 1596 CE (traditional founding); present structure ~150 years old
history.summary: SAME COMPLEX as seq 1603: this is the distinct Parvati shrine standing face-to-face with the Shiva shrine inside the Baba Basukinath Dham complex at Basukinath, Jarmundi block, Dumka district — NOT a separate independent temple, so treat as a related/same-complex record. It is a small white-marble shrine (described as ~5 m x 5 m, verify) whose doors align with the Shiva shrine's; per local belief the two doors are never opened simultaneously because Shiva and Parvati meet each evening, and the courtyard is cleared at dusk. It shares the complex's history, festivals and management. No shrine-specific photograph was found — the image below shows the Basukinath temple complex which houses this shrine.

name: Parvati Temple, Basukinath
town_description: Basukinath is a pilgrimage town in the Jarmundi block of Dumka district, Jharkhand, on the Deoghar-Dumka state highway. It exists essentially around the Baba Basukinath Dham temple complex and swells with Kanwariya pilgrims during Shravan. The Santhal Pargana region around it is one of Jharkhand's most important Hindu pilgrimage corridors, paired with Deoghar's Baidyanath Dham.

travel.airport: Deoghar Airport, ~50 km (verify); Dumka has no commercial airport
travel.railway: Deoghar Junction, ~45 km (verify); local Basukinath Halt nearby (verify)
travel.road: Inside the Baba Basukinath Dham complex on the Deoghar-Dumka highway, ~45 km from Deoghar

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Shravan (July-August) for the Kanwar mela (very crowded)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Same as the main complex: 5:00 AM-5:00 PM and 6:00 PM-11:00 PM (verify); shrine doors reportedly closed at dusk for the divine couple's evening meeting
